name: Popover
description: A small panel anchored to a trigger: it grows out of the trigger (the morph recipe), flips to the other side when there's no room, and closes on Escape, a press outside, or Tab past its last control, giving focus back to the trigger.
usage: Use for a few controls or a short read that belongs to one button: a worker count, notifications, a status line in full
Pass the trigger as a render prop and spread its props onto your own button (levain Button, an icon button, a name)
Uncontrolled by default; pass open and onOpenChange to control it
Pass children as a function to get close, for a control that finishes the job (Save, a pick)
Menu (T41) is a Popover with role="menu"; for a list of actions wait for Menu rather than building rows in a Popover
Not for a modal task (use Modal) or a hover hint (Tooltip, T42)
examples:
<Popover label="Workers" align="end" alignOffset={4} className="w-60"
  trigger={p => <Button {...p} variant="ghost" aria-label="Workers"><Users size={16} /></Button>}>
  <Slider label="Pool size" min={1} max={8} value={n} onChange={setN} />
</Popover>

// in a bar nothing clips: rendered beside the trigger, which shows over the surface as it morphs
<Popover portal={false} label="Project" trigger={p => <button {...p}>levain</button>}>...</Popover>
design: One surface: --color-surface-elevated, --elevation-3 with a 1px inset --color-border-subtle ring, --radius-lg corner
Opens as recipe.morph from the trigger's box to the panel's; content follows with contentIn after contentOut; closes with contentOut then recipe.collapse. Reduce Motion: a fade in place

Placed by calculatePopupPosition (utils/popupPosition): 6px from the trigger, start-aligned under it by default, flipped when the preferred side is short, kept viewportMargin (8px) inside the window, capped to the window's width
Portalled to the body at z-index 60, above Modal and the StatusCard dialogs (z-50)
Content padding 0.75rem and width to fit by default; className sets the content box (w-60, p-1)
accessibility: The trigger gets aria-haspopup (the role), aria-expanded, and aria-controls naming the panel while it's open
The panel has the role (dialog by default) and label as its accessible name
Focus moves in (initialFocus, else the first control, else the panel) and back to the trigger on close
Escape closes it via useDialogFocus: only the top layer answers, so a Popover in a Modal closes alone; a widget inside that claims Escape keeps it open
Not a focus trap: Tab past the last control or Shift+Tab before the first closes it, back to the trigger

props.name: trigger
props.description: Renders the trigger; spread the given ref, onClick and aria props onto a button.

props.name: children
props.description: The panel's content, or a function given close.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Leave out for uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the trigger, Escape, a press outside, Tab or close asks to open or close.

props.name: placement
props.description: The preferred side; flips to the opposite one when it has no room.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description: Gap from the trigger, in px.

props.name: alignOffset
props.description: How far the panel reaches past the trigger's aligned edge, in px (the board's panels use 4).

props.name: viewportMargin
props.description: Least distance from the window's edges, in px.

props.name: role
props.description: The panel's role, also the trigger's aria-haspopup.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description: What gets focus on open, instead of the first control.

props.name: portal
props.description: Portal to the body above dialogs (the default; use it everywhere else). false renders it beside the trigger, under it, but it is still position: fixed with viewport coordinates, so inside a transformed parent (a Modal, an animated container) it lands in the wrong place: use false only for a trigger in a static bar.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the panel's content box (padding, width).
